concepts.why: The patient's erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions and the mycological culture yielding growth of Trichophyton mentagrophytes support this diagnosis.
The patient's elevated eosinophil count and high IgE level, along with the presence of skin lesions, suggest this diagnosis.
The patient's skin lesions, high IgE level, and history of contact with stray cats, which may trigger allergies, support this diagnosis.
The mycological culture yielding growth of Trichophyton mentagrophytes and the patient's skin lesions support this diagnosis.
The patient's skin lesions and history of frequent contact with stray cats, which may cause allergic reactions, support this diagnosis.
The patient's skin lesions and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate support this diagnosis.
The patient's skin lesions and high IgE level support this diagnosis.
The patient's skin lesions and mycological culture yielding growth of Trichophyton mentagrophytes support this diagnosis.
The patient's skin lesions and elevated eosinophil count support this diagnosis.
The patient's skin lesions and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate support this diagnosis.

rationales.F04: Erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions are characteristic of dermatophytosis and other skin conditions.
rationales.F09: Eosinophilia is often seen in eosinophilic dermatitis and atopic dermatitis.
rationales.F10: High IgE levels are commonly found in atopic dermatitis.
rationales.F11: Mycological culture yielding Trichophyton mentagrophytes is diagnostic of dermatophytosis.

frontier_selector.rationale: Mycological culture yielded growth of Trichophyton mentagrophytes, which is a specific finding that strongly supports Trichophyton mentagrophytes infection as the diagnosis.
